notes.title: End of 2020
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36694415/d69208163a0b5488ed64705e7831bb859689b3e5.png[/img]

[h2]Hi fellow enthusiasts![/h2]

The year 2020 is near the end, so I'd like to wish you all Merry Christmas and Happy New Year 2021. The year 2020 was certainly not the best for many of us, but at least with regards to rocketry and space exploration it was not so bad! Here's short recap from last 2 months:

[b]🚀 Nov 16th - Falcon 9 / Space X Crew 1 mission:[/b] first commercial crewed operational flight performed by private company! Four astronauts were brought to ISS by SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket in Crew Dragon capsule, starting the new era of crewed spaceflight.

[b]🚀 Nov 23rd - Long March 5 / Chang'e 5 mission:[/b] Chinese mission to the Moon and back with return of lunar soil! The last time when lunar soil was returned back to Earth was in 1976! The launch was performed by Long March 5 rocket, the heaviest one in Chinese arsenal.

[b]🚀 Dec 9th - Starship SN8 test flight:[/b] spectacular 12.5 km hop of VTVL (vertical take-off, vertical landing) Starship prototype of SpaceX. It ended up in explosion, but Starship proven itself to be viable concept. Its landing flip is stunt of 2020 for me! SpaceX doesn't stop and that's goooood!

[b]🚀 Dec 13th - Angara A5 2nd test launch:[/b] Angara A5 is the new Russian heavy launch vehicle which aims to replace Proton and will be adapted also for crewed launches! This test launch was complete success and more are yet to come!

So not bad really, eh?

With Winter Holidays here and Steam Winter Sale running Universe Quiz is also participating, so if you are motivated to check your skills in astronomy and space exploration or learn something new a bit, Universe Quiz is in [b][u]discount[/u][/b].

And for the most hard-core enthusiast of you, I'm brewing something new related to space exploration and rockets. If you would like to, check the web of new project: [b][url=https://vdapps.net/universequest]Universe Quest[/url][/b].

That's all folks, one more time [b]Merry Christmas and Happy New Year 2021 to all of you![/b]

🚀🚀🚀

notes.title: Martian discount
notes.notes:
[h2]Hello Space Exploration Enthusiasts![/h2]

[b]This July[/b] was super-exciting month with [b]3 launches to Mars[/b]. I described them in more detail in my previous post. However, I was super-anxious, as no one can be 100% sure if some launch is not going to fail for some reason. And hey, space is not forgiving.

But hooray, all [b]3 spacecrafts[/b] were successfully placed into their trajectories with destination [b]Mars[/b] by their respective carrier rockets. Chronologically (on the image from left to right), [b]Hope[/b] spacecraft of [b]United Arab Emirates[/b] by [b]Japanese H-IIA[/b] rocket, [b]Chinese Tianwen-1[/b] spacecraft by [b]Long March 5[/b] rocket, and [b]Perseverance[/b] rover with [b]Ingenuity[/b] helicopter drone by [b]US Atlas V[/b] rocket.

To celebrate this successful month [b]Universe Quiz[/b] is on [b]40% discount[/b] starting on [b]July, 31st[/b] and valid for [b]14 days[/b]!

We can say, every one of those [b]3 Mars missions[/b] is now at middle of its journey. notes.title: Destination: Mars
notes.notes:
[h2]Hello Space Exploration Enthusiasts![/h2]

[b]This July[/b] is going to be super exciting month for space exploration. As [b]Mars[/b] is going to be in ideal position relative to [b]Earth[/b] to reach it with our rockets, there are several mission launches to [b]Mars[/b] planned this month. Let's recapitulate it, so you'll not miss any one of them:

[u][b]July, 14th:[/b][/u] [b]Hope Mars Mission[/b] or [b]Emirates Mars Mission[/b]. The result of co-operation between the [b]Mohammed bin Rashid Space Centre[/b] of [b]United Arab Emirates[/b] and 3 [b]US[/b] universities (the [b]University of Colorado Boulder[/b], [b]Arizona State University[/b] and the [b]University of California, Berkeley[/b]). The mission payload is an orbiter spacecraft called [b]Hope[/b], which aims to study [b]Mars[/b] atmosphere and its weather cycles. The mission will be launched by [b]Japanese H-IIA[/b] rocket. [i]Nice co-operation and glad to see another country to actively participate in deep space exploration![/i]

[u][b]July, 23rd:[/b][/u] [b]Tianwen-1[/b] mission. It is the first [b]Chinese[/b] attempt to soft-land on [b]Mars[/b], with lander and also rover as mission payloads. Apart of them, the mission contains also orbiter spacecraft which will circle around the [b]Mars[/b] and apart of doing scientific studies will serve also as data relay to communicate with the [b]Earth[/b]. The mission will be launched by the [b]Chinese[/b] most powerful rocket: [b]Long March 5[/b]. [i]Very ambitious![/i]

[u][b]July, 30th:[/b][/u] [b]NASA[/b]'s [b]Mars 2020[/b] mission with [b]Perseverance[/b] rover on board with [b]Ingenuity[/b] small robotic helicopter (yeah!) as its side-kick, which will scout surrounding area for the best targets to study! Just WOW! The goal of the mission is to search for possible biosignatures on [b]Mars[/b], and to collect samples to one place which will be retrieved later by future [b]Mars[/b] samples return mission. The mission will be launched by now classic, reliable and proven [b]Atlas V[/b] rocket. [i]Can't wait to see the first helicopter in action on different planet![/i]

So, are you excited? Me totally! And of course, if you want to know more about not just [b]Mars[/b], but also whole [b]Solar System[/b] and our [b]Universe[/b] in general, hey, here's the [b]Universe Quiz[/b] to play and to prove and boost your astronomy and space exploration knowledge.

See you at the [b]post missions recap[/b]! 

🚀🚀🚀

notes.title: Crew Dragon Demo-2 mission, T-minus one month..
notes.notes:
[h3][b]Hi space exploration enthusiasts![/b][/h3]

There are not many news regarding space launches these days, amidst coronavirus crisis. Most of them were post-poned. ːsteamsadː

But hey, there's one very significant launch, which is still on schedule! ːsteamhappyː

[b][u]SpaceX Crew Dragon Demo-2[/u][/b] mission is planned to launch at [b][u]May, 27th[/u][/b] to lift astronauts to International Space Station. If successfully launched, it will mean that for the first time after long [b]9 years[/b], manned space flight will be performed by other than super-reliable Russian [b]Soyuz [/b]rocket/spacecraft.

Moreover, it will be significant step forward, as spacecraft is much heavier, with more internal pressurized volume, it has significantly higher lift capacity of up to [b]7 astronauts plus cargo[/b] and the capsule is equipped with newest shiny high-tech.

Space exploration and spaceflight desperately need such kick forward!

Can't wait to see it! 🚀

[i](Image credit: SpaceX (public domain))[/i]
